title: Callum and the Light Game
markdown:
Dr. Ada’s workshop thrummed with a happy hum, a symphony of whirring gears and pinging springs. Sunlight, thick with dust motes, streamed through tall windows onto a scene of cheerful invention. Today the hum faltered.

“Oh, fiddlesticks and flutterbyes,” Dr. Ada cried, brow creased. Her Sunbeam Sorter, meant to sort sunshine by colour, was missing its heart: a small polished brass sphere. “It bounced, like a runaway golden bead, and vanished.” Her twinkling eyes clouded.

Callum, usually engrossed in quiet projects amidst bubbling beakers, peeked from behind blueprints. His bright eyes widened. “What’s wrong, Dr. Ada?”

Fern the hedgehog, a blur of bristly energy, scurried forward. Her sharp nose was renowned for finding grubs and berries, but this was a puzzle. The sphere had rolled into a rickety garden shed, its entrance half-collapsed by a fallen beam, plunging the interior into gloom. Fern wriggled through a gap. The sphere glinted behind the beam, just out of reach. She pushed with all her might. The beam was too heavy. A tiny hiss of frustration escaped her.

Callum peered into the shed’s dimness and saw Fern’s struggle. Then sunlight through a cracked window struck a metal watering can, sending a bright glint bouncing off its curve. It ricocheted off a shard of green glass, then, astonishingly, bounced again, landing on Callum’s coat button. A thought sparked.

“Hmm, I wonder,” Callum murmured, tracing the light’s playful path. “Fern, watch the beam. Just watch it.”

He scrambled back to Dr. Ada, his usual calm a little flustered. “Do you have your small mirror?”

“Of course, dear boy.” Dr. Ada produced a tiny silver-backed mirror. Callum took it, plus his fallen coat button and the green glass, and returned to the shed. Fern watched, whiskers quivering.

Callum held up the shiny button. He tilted his head. Sunlight leaped from the window, struck the button, and shot into the shed. He adjusted it. A millimetre here, a fraction of a degree there. The light beam moved, dancing into the gloom.

“It’s like a game of chase-the-light.”

He picked up the green glass. Sunlight hit its smooth surface and bent, guiding the light around a rusty bucket. Each bounce sent the light further. He was seeing around obstacles. Then the small mirror. He held it steady, hand surprisingly firm, and angled it. Sunlight bounced past the fallen beam, directly onto the lost brass sphere.

“There it is,” Fern squeaked, eyes shining. The sphere glowed brilliantly.

Callum pointed the mirror to a spot on the floor by the beam. “Dr. Ada. Right there. Lift from that spot.”

Hope in her eyes, she understood. She lifted the beam. With a groan it shifted. Fern, quick as a flash, wriggled through the new gap and nudged the sphere out.

Fern hopped with joy. Dr. Ada let out a whoop. She knelt beside Callum. “You used the very nature of light. You understood how it bounces.”

Callum felt a warmth spread through him, warmer than the sun. He had been worried about the mess, about the urgency, but his observant mind had found a way. Nervousness had not won.

“This little beauty works because of reflection,” Dr. Ada said, tapping the sphere. “Light bounces off surfaces, just like a ball bounces off a wall. By understanding angles, you can guide it. Telescopes. Periscopes. And of course,” she winked, “how my Sunbeam Sorter will sort sunshine into its rainbow.”

Callum looked at the shiny sphere, then the mirror, then the sunlight playing on the floor. The most remarkable solutions were often hidden in plain sight. He had overcome the little flutter of worry not by wishing it away, but by observing, experimenting, and trying something new. What wonders, he thought, might he discover next?
characters: Callum (a calm experimenter), Fern (a bristly puzzle-hedgehog), Dr. Ada Brook (a sunbeam-sorter inventor)
author: StoryGen Community
